title: Restore missing tenant metrics after obs-gateway heartbeat eclipse
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
During the 2026-02-03 incident a subset of tenants (hosted + dedicated pools) experienced intermittent metric/trace gaps and missing dashboard tiles for ~15-90 minutes. Symptoms were: lost time-series (zeroed or absent), live panels showing stale snapshots, and trace spans not stitched to metrics. This ticket implements a durable forwarding shim and graceful drain/eviction handling to prevent future 'heartbeat eclipse' gaps.

What happened (root cause hypothesis):
- Observability gateway (obs-gateway) emits periodic heartbeats and flushes batched telemetry to the ingest pipeline.
- Under a rapid scale-in event from the autoscaler (burst reclaim + preemption window), obs-gateway instances entered an eviction drain but a race between the heartbeat timer and the eviction pre-stop hook caused buffered batches to be dropped.
- Drops manifested as missing metric series and uncorrelated spans; depending on downstream shard assignment the missing data window varied per-tenant.
- Additional contributor: transient network routing during the autoscaler operation caused retries to be suppressed due to a client-side backoff matrix not honoring durable queue semantics.

High-level fix implemented in this ticket:
1) Agent/obs-gateway side durable spool: checkpoint batched telemetry to a local, append-only spool (fs-backed, small size, TTL) before announcing successful handoff to the network layer. On graceful shutdown, spool is drained synchronously; on unclean exit, next startup replays the spool to the ingest gateway.
2) Forwarding shim: small process that accepts batched telemetry over unix socket and performs idempotent forward with at-least-once semantics. This isolates heartbeat scheduling from network handoff.
3) Eviction/drain improvements: add an autoscaler pre-evict annotation and ensure the agent honors a 15s pre-stop drain window; add explicit drain hooks that flush the spool.
4) Backoff matrix change: allow a short jittered retry window during scale operations and treat 5xx responses as transient for spool replay.
5) Observability: new internal metric obs_gateway.spool_drain_latency and gauge obs_gateway.spool_unreplayed_count; dashboard panels for spool health and pre-evict events.

Rollback/compatibility strategy:
- The shim is opt-in via a config flag and will be rolled into a small canary cohort (10% of gateways) for 24h before global rollout. Can revert by turning flag off and restarting agents in cohort.

Why this is different from previous fixes:
- Prior fixes focused on aggregation windows and index rehydration. This addresses the producer-side loss mode (pre-network drop) at the edge of hosted/dedicated/private deployments and adds a durable local guard to guarantee eventual delivery of in-flight batches.
notes:
Testing done:
- Unit tests for spool write/rotate and replay semantics.
- Integration tests with local ingest mock; verified at-least-once delivery across restarts and simulated preemptions.
- Load test: 10k tenants simulated; spool size tuned to 64MB per process with evict/drain latency under 200ms for 99th percentile during normal load.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: deploy shim behind config flag to canary cohort (10%). Monitor obs_gateway.spool_unreplayed_count and dashboard for any increase in latency.
- Stage 2: expand to 50% after 24h if no regression.
- Stage 3: full rollout and deprecate old behavior.

Communication:
- Incident report drafted for customers impacted, currently being reviewed by support/ops.
- Postmortem will include timeline, RCA, and steps for customers to validate restored metrics in their dashboards.
